analysis.title: Can The AI Rally Survive Nvidia Without Jensen?
key_insights: Nvidia's board announced Thursday Nov 12, 2026 that Jensen Huang resigned as President, CEO and director effective immediately. CFO Colette Kress becomes interim CEO while keeping the CFO role, Harvey C. Jones becomes first-ever Chair, and the search for a permanent CEO will consider internal and external candidates.
NVDA fell 10% from the prior close to its lowest since July 2025 and more than 35% below its highs. The stock had already lost about a third of its value in a month.

Goldman's Rich Privorotsky (EMEA Delta One) wrote before the resignation that the rally was 'emphatically not a broad based move'. SOX rose 5.5%, ARM and MU each rose 12%, while MSFT, META and AMZN finished lower. S&P rose 1.3% to 7,619, Nasdaq 100 rose 2.3%, Russell rose 0.9%, Dow rose 0.5%.

Goldman's Retail Favorites basket (GSXURFAV) rose 495bps, its 3rd best day in three years, with Treasuries closed for Veterans Day. Three stocks priced under $4 accounted for 32% of US tape volume. The basket faded from +6.46% intraday to +4.95%.

Goldman Prime desk: systematic L/S funds rose 1.25% Wednesday, a +2.6 standard deviation move with about three-quarters of funds up, driven by momentum renormalization and recovery in crowded trades. Privo says systematic L/S managers posted their best two-day return in nearly three years (+2.15%).

Privo says the vol complex has largely reset: SPX vol curve un-inverted and dealer skew flattened. Derivatives desk (Shayna Peart) described a shift from last week's panic to this week's complacency, with VIX down 992bps to 17.53 and Thursday's SPX straddle priced at 57bps. Investors are buying December SPX call spreads toward peak dealer gamma near 7,800.

Privo's open question is whether the rally is the mechanical result of low positioning and short covering or the start of something durable. Callahan says there is relatively little consensus, with debate over a bear market bounce versus a forming bull market.

Privo's view is that a durable breakout probably requires lower rates, lower energy and broader leadership. Absent that he expects chop rather than breakout, though low positioning and high vol are short-term tailwinds.

On AI infrastructure Privo separates compute demand from valuation multiples. Hyperscalers are best positioned given balance sheets and contracted infrastructure. He expects episodic, high-beta trading rallies rather than buy-and-hold, with strong micro results coexisting with multiple compression.

Privo's four AI overhangs: higher cost of capital, power and permitting constraints, supply/demand balance entering 2028, and monetization velocity relative to capex. Near-term permitting and logistics worries have eased, but the real worries are long-term supply absorption and ROI realization.
Goldman economists now expect a third rate hike in March 2027, per the article's author.

Iran: Privo sees conflicting headlines, including a contentious Netanyahu-Trump call (disputed by Netanyahu's office), Vance exploring direct talks Tehran has resisted, and Iranian claims of roughly a two-week window before US military action decisions. A third US carrier group is heading to the region, possibly arriving mid-month.

Russia/Ukraine: Polymarket odds of a ceasefire by December have fallen toward 10%, and about 25% by March. Abu Dhabi talks produced agreement in principle on a prisoner exchange but little progress on territorial and security questions.

Goldman's Euro Area 2027 Consumer Outlook: real retail sales measures have fallen to about -0.5% on a 3m/3m basis. Real consumption growth is seen stalling near 0% qoq over the winter, with 0.1% qoq in H1 2027 and 0.2% in H2.

The article author is skeptical of Privo's 'low positioning and high vol are tailwinds' point. The author calls the setup a bear market rally fingerprint (short covering, 57bp straddle, penny stocks at a third of volume, NVDA losing its CEO). Goldman's credit monitor shows USD CCC spreads at 1,098bps, up 270bps in three months and near the 3-year max of 1,127bps.

Nvidia reports earnings Tuesday Nov 17 with Kress as interim CEO and CFO. Wedbush's Dan Ives says Nvidia is worth 25% less without Huang. Before the announcement Nasdaq futures were down 1.5% and S&P futures down 0.7%.

tension_points.bull_case: Positioning has been reset materially, vol remains elevated and the market has absorbed an extraordinary amount of bad news. Privo calls low positioning and high vol powerful short-term tailwinds, and rotation within AI continues without leaving the theme.
tension_points.bear_case: Breadth is narrow, the rally is short-covering driven, and a 57bp straddle plus penny-stock volume fit a bear market rally. NVDA is leaderless heading into earnings, CCC spreads are near 3-year highs, and the Fed is hiking into an oil shock.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A broad capitulation or failure of rotation within AI after the Nvidia news (Thursday is the test), or Nvidia's Nov 17 earnings call failing to settle governance questions.

tension_points.bull_case: Privo sees plenty of reasons to be constructive, with low positioning and high vol as tailwinds.
tension_points.bear_case: A durable breakout probably requires lower rates, lower energy and broader leadership, and without those Privo suspects the market chops rather than breaks out.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Oil prices falling and rates coming lower together, which Privo says is what the market needs.
